body.x: ROBOTIS Co., Ltd. (CEO Byengsoo Kim) participated in the “HUMANOID M.AX Alliance” pavilion at CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9.

ROBOTIS leads the physical AI market through core technologies it has successfully localized, including actuators (DYNAMIXEL) and reducers. With technological capabilities that cover the entire process of robot actuation, control, and autonomous driving, the company has built a portfolio spanning from core components to finished products.

Its major businesses include modular actuators, which have become a standard in robot development; finished robot products, such as the dual-arm humanoid “AI Worker,” which enables precise tasks through imitation and reinforcement learning; and the autonomous delivery robot “GAEMI.”

Beyond simple hardware manufacturing, ROBOTIS has also begun scaling up its “data factory” business, which processes and sells behavioral data collected by intelligent robots. By securing “action data,” a core element of VLA models, and advancing hardware performance, the company is moving toward becoming a global platform company.

At CES 2026, ROBOTIS showcased precision manipulation technology through its semi-humanoid “AI Worker.” AI Worker is a dual-arm task-oriented humanoid robot that combines hardware technology based on ROBOTIS’s high-performance actuators, DYNAMIXEL, with artificial intelligence. The company explained that, using physical AI technology, the robot goes beyond simple repetition to perform human-level skilled work.

In particular, the robot features an intelligent learning mechanism that combines imitation learning, which follows a worker’s movements in real time, with reinforcement learning through simulation. Through this approach, AI Worker autonomously optimizes and performs high-difficulty processes such as logistics and distribution, assembly, welding, and inspection.

body.cap: ROBOTIS’s semi-humanoid “AI Worker” follows a worker’s movements in real time. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In addition, by mounting its in-house-developed DYNAMIXEL actuators, the robot handles irregularly shaped or moving objects with a flexible, precise approach. High accessibility is also a key feature. Even non-robot experts can deploy the robot immediately on site through intuitive operation, maximizing automation efficiency while addressing labor shortages in industrial environments.

Furthermore, AI Worker serves as a core hub of the “data factory,” generating and accumulating high-quality action data through task execution, and it functions as an essential platform for developing AI foundation models.

ROBOTIS generates approximately 80 percent of its total revenue from overseas markets, establishing itself as a global robotics specialist. It currently operates local subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China, building a robust global supply chain that spans worldwide markets.

Its major export regions include North America, Asia, and Europe, which are key hubs of the robotics industry. According to company representatives, the largest export item is DYNAMIXEL, a robot-dedicated actuator that supplies leading global robotics companies and research institutes, and has gained recognition as a global standard for robot drive systems.

body.cap: Visitors at CES 2026 observe the movements of ROBOTIS’s semi-humanoid “AI Worker.” | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Recently, global demand for the task-oriented humanoid “AI Worker,” a next-generation growth driver, has reportedly surged. As interest in finished products incorporating physical AI technology increases, ROBOTIS accelerates its global market share by combining the stability of its component business with the growth potential of finished robots.

A ROBOTIS official said, “Through our own hardware platforms such as ‘AI Worker,’ we secure action data and establish a virtuous cycle in which the collected data feeds back into enhancing robot performance. By serving as an ‘action data hub,’ ROBOTIS plans to firmly position itself not merely as a component supplier, but as a global robot platform company leading the era of physical AI and a true game changer in the market.”

The HUMANOID M.AX Alliance is a public-private consultative body formed in April 2025 with the participation of 260 organizations and companies, including AI research institutes, robot manufacturers, component suppliers, and universities and research institutions. The alliance jointly promotes the demonstration and commercialization of AI-based humanoids in industrial environments. At CES 2026, the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion went beyond simple product displays and presented a practical model for ecosystem building by connecting AI, platform, and component technologies.
